foundational_principle: God convicts us so that he can comfort us. He exposes our delusions of self-sufficiency so that we will turn from our sin and turn to him for salvation.

points.title: Introducing Isaiah
points.content: Isaiah's name means "The Lord Saves." His prophetic ministry directly addresses our problem and God's provision.

sub_points.label: A
sub_points.title: Confrontation
sub_points.content: Sin deceives our hearts and distorts our perspective. The first step in salvation is a recognition of our true condition.

sub_points.label: B
sub_points.title: Accusation
bullets: They are stubborn and senseless, forgetting God's faithful care.
They are proud and polluted, forsaking God who satisfies.
They are desperate and desolate, but think they can save themselves.

sub_points.label: C
sub_points.title: Glimpse of Grace
sub_points.content: Their rebellion deserves God's destruction, but God offers salvation because of his mercy.

points.title: Repentance
points.content: When convicted of sin, we can either conceal it or confess it. One compounds our guilt; the other cleanses it.

sub_points.label: A
sub_points.title: Conceal
sub_points.content: God is disgusted by worship that is hollow and hypocritical. He hates every form of worship that does not flow from a heart of humility and repentance.

sub_points.label: B
sub_points.title: Confess
sub_points.content: God's accusation is followed by an invitation to repent. He calls us to honestly confess and urgently forsake our sin.

sub_points.label: A
sub_points.title: Sobering Reflection
sub_points.content: God uses shocking language to awaken them to the severity of their condition and the stubbornness of their pride.

sub_points.label: B
sub_points.title: Stunning Redemption
sub_points.content: God will punish them in order to purify them. He will redeem and restore hopeless sinners through his justice and by his grace.

sub_points.label: C
sub_points.title: Stubborn Refusal
sub_points.content: Those who resist conviction and refuse salvation will be objects of God's judgment rather than recipients of his grace.
